leg: five-bar (leg v2, cad/fivebar.py): l1 150 mm, l2 250 mm, motors 150 mm apart

wheel.route: hub (inner end, at the axle) -> under the apex eye -> along the wheel link's outer edge -> round the outside of the rear knee -> along the rear upper link's outer edge -> into the body 90 mm from the hip axis (fivebar.cable)

length_mm.note: the spread over the stances: what the knee wrap and the loop at the hip must give

bend_radius.note: the drawn spline's tightest bend, against 10 x the 18 AWG conductor (rule 3, flexing). At every stance it is where the route turns off the rear upper link's edge into the body (fivebar.cable()'s last three waypoints, 5 mm then 35 mm apart): the drawn route needs a wider turn there before it is a harness drawing

lead_length.note: the BotWheel's own lead is 300 mm; the route ends where it enters the body, so the run on to the motor driver inside is extra

clash.note: parts the swept Ø9 cable runs into (> 5 mm3), motors and the hub left out

front.route: rear cover (XT30 + CAN) on the hip frame -> into the body

rear.route: rear cover (XT30 + CAN) on the hip frame -> into the body

limits: a drawn route, not a measured cable: clips are not drawn, and the rig decides (docs/mechanical-interfaces.md)
